ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a simple power system equivalent circuit. On the left side is the internal potential E′, and to the right, reactances j0.295 and j0.138 are connected in series in sequence; in the middle there are two branches labeled j0.486 connected in parallel; further to the right, reactance j0.122 is connected in series, reaching the terminal voltage bus. The upper right indicates the terminal voltage U=1.0∠0°, and the lower right indicates the operating power P0=1.0, cosφ=0.98. Reasoning calculation: The two j0.486 are in parallel, and the equivalent reactance is j0.486/2=j0.243. Therefore the total reactance XΣ=0.295+0.138+0.243+0.122=0.798 p.u. From P0=1.0, cosφ=0.98, get Q0=P0 tan(arccos 0.98)≈0.203. Take U=1∠0, then the current I≈1−j0.203. The internal potential E′=U+jXΣI=1+j0.798(1−j0.203)≈1.162+j0.798, so |E′|≈sqrt(1.162^2+0.798^2)≈1.41. The power limit Pmax=|E′|U/XΣ≈1.41/0.798≈1.77. The static stability reserve coefficient K_P=(Pmax−P0)/P0×100%≈(1.77−1.0)/1.0×100%≈77%.
